title: Sandbox ribbon: first-project wizard and micro-coaching for Console empty states
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: New Console users land on empty project pages and abandon before creating a workload because they don't know which first steps reduce cost or validate results. Current starter templates feel generic and don't teach trade-offs (latency vs cost) or show rollouts/observability patterns.

Goal: Design a lightweight "sandbox ribbon" (persistent strip at top of project empty states) that surfaces a 3-step first-project wizard + contextual micro-coaching cards. The ribbon should bootstrapped with a sample workload (text gen demo) and offer one-click playground, recommended cost settings (batching, sequence length), and a clear path to enable rollouts and metrics. The design must: 1) reduce time-to-first-request, 2) teach 2 cost levers, and 3) encourage enabling Rollouts/Tracing within the first session.

Proposed solution: A horizontal ribbon with three states: Setup -> Run -> Observe. Each state shows a short microtask, an inline CTA (button or toggle), and a tiny explainer. Ribbon will include: a persistent "Try sample workload" button that opens an in-page sandbox with prefilled prompt + token budget; a cost-preview microcard that shows estimated cost per 1k tokens under current settings and a recommended toggle to enable batching/quantization; and a lightweight rollout checklist linking to canary rollout preset. Copy will use plain language and emphasize safety (no billing surprises) and reversibility.

Design deliverables: low-fi flows, high-fi ribbon component in Figma, 3 micro-coaching card variants (cost, rollouts, observability), accessibility QA checklist, and a short prototype for moderated testing.

Success metrics: move Time-to-first-request from 18% activation -> target 35% within 6 weeks for new orgs; increase users who enable rollouts within 14 days from 4% -> 12%; 10% reduction in support tickets tagged "where to start" for first 30 days.
acceptance_criteria: Ribbon component implemented in Figma with responsive rules for narrow viewports
Prototype demonstrates first-project flow: Setup -> Run -> Observe with working sandboxes
Micro-coaching card copy reviewed and signed off by PM and Legal for billing language
Design tokens and accessibility color contrast meet WCAG AA
Interaction spec includes success/fail states and analytics hooks for activation, cost-toggle, and rollout opt-in
comments: 2026-03-03 - Ava Martinez: Kicked off design spike. Ran 3 quick interviews with new users from trial orgs. Common quote: 'I don't know where to click or what the right settings are.'
2026-03-04 - Liam O'Connor: Early exploration attached in Figma. Suggest we keep ribbon height <= 64px to avoid pushing key console chrome down. Also flagged mobile collapse behavior.

2026-03-05 - Priya Narang (PM): Love the Setup->Run->Observe metaphor. PM asks that cost preview uses conservative estimates and includes a 'why this matters' tooltip. Also requests analytics events for 'toggle batching' and 'enable rollout'.

2026-03-06 - Security review (Jake Turner): Billing copy must include link to pricing page and explicit note that sandbox runtime uses free tier credits when applicable. No sensitive data surfaced in sample workloads.

2026-03-08 - Design review with Engineering: Agreed on a progressive disclosure approach for technical knobs (advanced settings hidden behind 'tweak performance'). Engineering warned about KV cache warmup latency for sample runs; recommended pre-warming strategy in runtime brief.

2026-03-09 - Usability test (moderated, n=6): 5/6 participants completed sample run within 3 minutes. Feedback: micro-coaching cards are helpful but some users wanted a one-click 'reset sample' button. Added to TODOs.

2026-03-10 - Liam O'Connor: Updated high-fi to include 'reset sample' and a minimal cost-savings calculation. Next: handoff ticket to ENG with interaction spec and analytics hooks (ENG dependency added).
